After 1 month, the patient responded to this treatment becoming seizure free and showing significant improvement in his cognitive state. He achieved an MMSE score of 27/30. clinician.final_diagnosis: VGKC-complex antibody limbic encephalitis with LGI1 as the specific antigenic target
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 59-year-old man presented with a 5-month progressive neuropsychiatric syndrome characterized by faciobrachial dystonic seizures (FBDS, 30-50/day), short-term memory impairment (MMSE 15/30), behavior disturbances, visual hallucinations, insomnia, and myoclonus. Initial workup revealed normal brain MRI (no hippocampal lesions), non-specific EEG findings (background slowing without periodic discharges), and normal CSF. Serum testing confirmed high titers of VGKC-complex antibodies (678.3 pmol/L) with LGI1 identified as the specific antigenic target and negative CASPR2 antibodies. Paraneoplastic screening identified benign intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasia (IPMN) of the pancreas without malignancy. The patient received intravenous immunoglobulin (0.4 g/kg daily for 5 days), achieving seizure freedom and significant cognitive improvement (MMSE 27/30) after one month. He remained relapse-free during 18-month follow-up with progressive reduction of antiepileptic therapy.

Normal brain MRI without hippocampal lesions

High serum VGKC-complex antibody titers (678.3 pmol/L, positive >85 pmol/L) with LGI1 as specific antigenic target and negative CASPR2 antibodies confirming autoimmune etiology
Paraneoplastic workup revealed benign pancreatic IPMN without malignancy, excluding paraneoplastic cause
Treatment response to IVIG (0.4 g/kg x 5 days) with seizure freedom, cognitive improvement (MMSE 15/30 to 27/30), and sustained remission over 18 months
